items.title: Bobby Hutcherson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Working right down the street was Lennie . . . [INTERVIEWER] Lennie Bruce? [INTERVIEWEE] Lennie Bruce. Ciro’s right across the street.

ctx.x: Can we go back? I was going to say, what happened after that concert, after your performance debut?

I realized either two things: I was either going to lay there on the floor, from getting decked like that, from that Sunday punch, and have everybody at school say, “See, I told you,” or I was going to get up off the canvas and make my mother proud. So me and Herbie, we started hanging out with Terry – what was Terry’s last name? He lived over in Glendale. We used to go over to his house and sit there and listen to records. Gee, I can’t remember the name. I can’t remember Terry’s name. You know what they say…

items.title: Bobby Hutcherson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Then Lenny Bruce came. Lenny Bruce, he had to say a whole bunch of stuff about Marilyn Monroe walking out...

ctx.x: I was working with Curtis Amy, Carmell Jones, Frank Butler – ooo, Frank Butler – at the Renaissance, opposite Lenny Bruce. We’re playing. It’s the end – kind of the end of the night. Nobody’s in there. All of a sudden Marilyn Monroe walks in with her entourage, and we’re playing One More Ham Hog Please. Curtis, he just loved to play, and Frank’s playing. Frank is one of these persons, he didn’t miss the scene. Anything happened, he checked it out right away. Curtis too. Eyes would be – first he sees these two…
